curriculum: The Dutch-taught Human Movement Sciences BSc is a 180 EC degree with a common curriculum. Articles 4.1 and 7.1 verify twelve 5 EC first-year components and the 120 EC post-propaedeutic curriculum. The 2026–27 poster distinguishes Movement Analysis 1 and 2, Skills Lab, Neuroanatomy 1 and 2, and Statistics 1, 2 and 3 where the public table repeats or mislabels entries. Eleven 5 EC courses, 3 EC orientation and 2 EC Bachelor Monitor account for 60 EC in the comparison’s second-year grouping. Monitor runs across years two and three and is counted once. Year three includes a genuine 15 EC minor, five 5 EC modules and a 20 EC research project. Articles 7.1 and 8.1 allow minor study, placement or study abroad, subject to applicable approval.
progression: The first year introduces anatomy, general physiology, neurophysiology, biomechanics, motor control, mathematics, programming and research methods. Later courses add exercise testing, laboratory measurement, motor development, neuroanatomy and movement interventions. Article 5.2 gives the 45 EC first-year binding study advice threshold, and Art. 5.7 addresses access to later years. Article 9.3 requires all 60 first-year EC and 43 second-year EC by the graduation-project application deadline. The current BWB306 catalog instead lists 45 second-year EC and the same first-year requirement and deadlines (1 December for February, 15 July for September). The comparison explicitly distinguishes the sources and uses the stricter 45 EC for planning. The modeled 60 EC in year two satisfies either threshold. The project includes supervised research, a report and presentation.

Both sources require all 60 EC from year one by the application deadline. The regulations specify 43 EC from year two, while the course catalog lists 45 EC. Plan for 45 EC from year two to meet both published thresholds.
